text:
elaine: Heads-up — I started a run reproducing the long-tail latency when tenant lanes get fragmented. Not a full outage but 95p spikes for small tenants. Repro steps and a couple logs below.

 tomas: Any recent changes to admission or preemption? :thinking_face:

 devon: Not on admission. We did tweak coalesce window sizes last week (small bump).

 elaine: I think it's an invariant-splintering problem: when a cohort's requests are split across many tiny queues, each queue's headroom gets depleted by larger tenants. Results in starvation even though aggregate capacity is underutilized.

 kevin: Can you outline the invariants you're worried about so we can reason about mitigations?

 elaine: Simplified: 1) fairness budget is allocated per-queue; 2) queues are short-lived and spawn frequently; 3) splitting creates many queues -> per-queue min-credit becomes tiny -> preemptive evictions and thrash -> small requests wait behind refill windows.

 tomas: That matches what I've seen in the traces. Symptoms: high queue_spawn_rate, high preempt_evictions on small tenants. Options I see: raise min-credit, lengthen queue_lifetime, or introduce a shared microqueue for short flows.

 devon: I'm leaning to making queues longer-lived + a compactor that merges low-util queues periodically. Raising min-credit helps but penalizes bursty large flows.

 elaine: Experiment config I ran locally (quick YAML):
```yaml
scheduler:
  queue_lifetime_ms: 200
  compactor_interval_ms: 5000
  min_credit_tokens: 8
  compact_threshold: 0.12
```
Results: 95p latency down ~18% for the affected tenant mix, p50 bumped ~+2ms. So tradeoff looks promising.

 kevin: Good datapoint. If we pursue compaction path we should add metrics: queue_count_by_tenant, queue_spawn_rate, compaction_merges, preempt_evictions, avg_queue_lifetime. Also add an SLO guard for p95 across tenant tiers.

 infra-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout/compact-experiment -> canary on 3 hosts at 2026-03-22T16:20:00Z

 elaine: @tomas can you own the canary? I'll post dashboards and a small toggle script to flip the config.

 tomas: On it. Quick design q: should compactor be centralized or per-host? Centralized is deterministic but adds a network dependency; per-host is fast and local but may be non-deterministic across hosts.

 devon: Per-host compaction with occasional global sweep seems pragmatic: local merges reduce churn quickly, global pass fixes cross-host fragmentation anomalies.

 kevin: Also think about compaction safety: ensure compact merges only combine queues when the merged token estimate < some threshold to avoid creating giant queues that amplify interference.

 elaine: Agreed. I'll draft an RFC follow-up covering: compactor lifecycle, merge safety checks, eviction backoff, and the new telemetry (Kevin's list). Will ping for review.

 kevin: SGTM. If canary looks stable we can promote to dedicated rollout and then prod after 48h of stable telemetry.

 elaine: Thanks all :thumbsup:
